name: Carbon Emissions Benchmark for Machine Translation
description: In recent times, there has been definitive progress in the field of NLP, with its applications growing as the utility of our language models increases with advances in their performance. However, these models require a large amount of computational power and data to train, consequently leading to large carbon footprints. Therefore, it is imperative that we study the carbon efficiency and look for alternatives to reduce the overall environmental impact of training models, in particular large language models. In our work, we assess the performance of models for machine translation, across multiple language pairs to assess the difference in computational power required to train these models for each of these language pairs and examine the various components of these models to analyze aspects of our pipeline that can be optimized to reduce these carbon emissions.
evaluation_method: BLEU (or other MT quality metrics) combined with carbon/emissions measurements (e.g., kgCO2eq per training run) — often reported as quality-per-emissions or separate BLEU and emissions values
general_score_metric: BLEU and carbon emissions (kgCO2eq) — often combined as a quality-per-emissions metric
reputation: Niche but important in the efficiency and sustainability research community; cited in works examining environmental impact of NLP training.
notes: Carbon measurements vary with hardware, datacenter, region, and measurement methodology; results are sensitive to experimental setup and are not directly comparable unless measurement protocols are standardized.
